description: "How NCodeGroup code implements OAuth 2.x, OpenID Connect, JOSE and related HTTP protocols, on both the server and the client side: request validation, token issuance and validation, discovery metadata, client registration, logout, sender-constrained tokens, error responses, rate limiting, and wire-format encoding."
applyTo: "**/*.cs, **/*.ts, **/*.tsx, **/*.cshtml, **/*.html"

# Protocols

<!-- Generated by `npm run train` from the sources each rule cites. To change a rule for good, change its source or say so in training/feedback.md; the next training run regenerates this file. -->

- **Carry an accepted redirect URI as the original string everywhere it is stored, compared or serialized. Refuse a request that has more than one `redirect_uri` value. At the token endpoint, compare `redirect_uri` with the value bound to the code using ordinal comparison, and treat an empty value as missing.** RFC 6749 §4.1.3 requires the values to be identical. A parsed `Uri` is normalized (lower-cased host, trailing slash), and multiple values joined into one string weaken the exact-match check. *Check:* Look for redirect URI fields or DTOs typed as `Uri`, serialization through `Uri.ToString()`/`AbsoluteUri`, multiple values joined together or the first one taken, and token-endpoint comparisons that use `Uri` equality or ignore case. <sub>Identity ADR-0203</sub>
- **When building an authorization response, keep the registered redirect URI's query pairs exactly as written, let a response parameter replace a registered parameter with the same name, and append the response parameters. Never copy request-supplied query parameters into it.** RFC 6749 §3.1.2 requires the registered query to be kept, and request-supplied query parameters must not reach the client. *Check:* Look for response writers that drop the registered query, duplicate parameters with the same name, reorder or re-encode existing pairs, or add query parameters taken from the request. <sub>Identity ADR-0203</sub>
- **Validate the redirect target, including that `redirect_uri` is registered, at the pushed authorization request endpoint when the request is pushed, not only later at the authorization endpoint.** RFC 9126 §2.1 expects the PAR endpoint to refuse a redirect URI that is not registered. *Check:* Look for PAR handling that stores a request without resolving and validating its redirect URI and response delivery. <sub>Identity ADR-0202</sub>
- **Do not support or advertise the PKCE `plain` method, and do not apply a default when a `code_challenge` arrives without `code_challenge_method`. Validate `code_challenge` and `code_verifier` against RFC 7636 syntax (43–128 unreserved characters). Return `invalid_request` for a missing or malformed challenge. Return `invalid_grant` for a missing, malformed or mismatched verifier, and for a verifier presented with a code that has no PKCE binding.** OAuth 2.1 forbids `plain` and requires the method. RFC 9700 §4.8.2 describes a verifier sent for an unbound code as a PKCE downgrade. *Check:* Look for `plain` constants or metadata, a default method fallback, missing length or character-set checks, `unauthorized_client` returned for PKCE failures, or a verifier ignored when the code has no challenge. <sub>Identity ADR-0144</sub>
- **In OAuth client code, send PKCE with S256 and a fresh random `state` (and a `nonce` when `openid` is requested) on every authorization-code request, make `code_verifier` mandatory on the code redemption, and verify the ID token's `nonce` against the stored value. Never create a session or tokens from an authorization response that carries `error`.** PKCE, state and nonce bind the callback and the ID token to the request that started them, which prevents injection and replay. *Check:* Look for authorize URL builders without `code_challenge_method=S256` or without state/nonce, reused values, an optional `code_verifier` in code-redemption types, ID tokens accepted without a nonce comparison, or callbacks that continue after an `error` parameter. <sub>Identity ADR-0082; Identity ADR-0270; Identity docs/backend-for-frontend.md</sub>
- **In client code, reject a provider whose `code_challenge_methods_supported` is present but does not include `S256`. Accept the provider when the list is absent.** The client only supports S256, and an absent list does not mean the provider lacks it. *Check:* Look for discovery checks that fail on an absent list, or that skip the check when a present list has no S256. <sub>Identity ADR-0275</sub>
- **In an authorization-code callback, pin the expected issuer in the login transaction and check the RFC 9207 `iss` response parameter against it before exchanging the code, whenever the provider advertises `authorization_response_iss_parameter_supported`. Delete the login-transaction cookie on every path, and always mint a new session handle.** Checking `iss` first prevents mix-up attacks, clearing the cookie leaves no reusable login state, and a fresh handle prevents session fixation. *Check:* Look for a code exchange before the `iss` check, `iss` ignored or compared with something other than the transaction's issuer, error paths that keep the login cookie, or a session that reuses a pre-login handle. <sub>Identity ADR-0290; Identity docs/backend-for-frontend.md</sub>
- **Enforce single use of one-time protocol values such as OAuth `state` by atomically taking (read-and-delete) the stored transaction from shared storage before decrypting or validating it.** An atomic take makes the value single-use on every replica, and nobody can probe the same transaction twice. *Check:* Look for callbacks that read, validate or decrypt, and then delete in a separate step, or that enforce single use only in local memory. <sub>Identity ADR-0290</sub>
- **Validate every requested scope at both the authorization endpoint and the token endpoint against the client's allowed-scope set, and reject any scope outside that set with `invalid_scope` instead of silently dropping it.** Entitlements mean nothing unless every request path enforces them. *Check:* Look for request validators that skip scope validation, validate on only one endpoint, return a different error code, or quietly filter out unauthorized scopes. <sub>Identity ADR-0026</sub>
- **Compare OAuth scope tokens case-sensitively with ordinal comparison.** RFC 6749 defines scope tokens as case-sensitive strings. *Check:* Look for scope sets or comparisons that use `OrdinalIgnoreCase`, `InvariantCultureIgnoreCase`, culture-aware equality, or `ToLower`/`ToUpper` normalization. <sub>Identity ADR-0026</sub>
- **Treat a scope as owned by exactly one resource server, so its identity is the pair (resource server, value). Never look up, constrain or match a scope by its value alone across resource servers.** The same scope name can mean different things on different APIs. *Check:* Look for scope queries, uniqueness constraints or comparisons keyed only on the scope value. <sub>Identity ADR-0023</sub>
- **Set an access token's `aud` to the distinct identifiers of the enabled resource servers that own its effective scopes, not to the client id. When `resource` parameters are sent, narrow the audience to them. When none are sent, keep the full scope-derived audience. Fall back to the client id only when no resource server applies, so `aud` is never empty.** `aud` must name the party that will accept the token. If it is the client id, a token minted for API A is accepted by API B. An access token must never lack an audience. *Check:* Look for issuance code that sets `aud` to the client id while resource servers apply, includes disabled resource servers, emits duplicates, can produce an empty or missing `aud`, or changes the default when no `resource` is requested. <sub>Identity ADR-0027; Identity ADR-0078</sub>
- **Reject with `invalid_target` any requested `resource` that is not a known, enabled resource server or that owns none of the token's effective scopes. Treat `resource` as a repeated parameter and match its values ordinally.** RFC 8707 requires invalid resources to be rejected with `invalid_target`. Resource identifiers must match exactly. *Check:* Look for code that silently drops unknown resources, returns `invalid_request`/`invalid_scope` for them, reads only the first `resource`, or compares with case-insensitive, culture-aware or URI-normalizing equality. <sub>Identity ADR-0078</sub>
- **Keep an ID token's `aud` equal to the client id, and apply scope-derived audiences only to access tokens.** OpenID Connect requires the ID token audience to be the client. *Check:* Look for ID tokens sent through resource-server audience resolution, or ID tokens whose `aud` is anything other than the client id. <sub>Identity ADR-0027</sub>
- **Serialize `aud` as a JSON string when there is one audience and as a JSON array when there are several.** RFC 7519 allows either form, and a token spanning several resource servers needs the array. *Check:* Look for encoders that always write an array, or that join several audiences into one string or keep only the first. <sub>Identity ADR-0027</sub>
- **Emit the server-owned stable principal id as `sub` and never pass through a raw upstream subject. Persist, key and resolve grants, consent, sessions and revocation by that internal id, and apply the pairwise `sub` projection only where the subject leaves the server in a token or response.** Relying parties get one durable subject per person. Internal joins such as revoke-all-for-user break if a pairwise value replaces the internal id. *Check:* Look for issuance or introspection that copies an external `sub`, and for grant, consent or session records stored or looked up by a projected pairwise `sub`. <sub>Identity ADR-0035; Identity ADR-0093</sub>
- **Have UserInfo return the `sub` already carried by the access token instead of projecting the subject again.** This keeps the UserInfo `sub` identical to the ID token `sub`, as OpenID Connect Core requires. *Check:* Look for UserInfo code that recomputes or re-projects `sub`. <sub>Identity ADR-0093</sub>
- **At the end-session endpoint, resolve the stable subject only from server-owned state: the session grant found by `sid`, falling back to the OP login cookie. Take only `sid` and `azp`/`aud` from `id_token_hint`, and never its `sub`.** For pairwise clients the hint's `sub` is a pseudonym. Using it matches no grants and projects the `sub` in back-channel logout tokens twice, which silently breaks logout. *Check:* Look for logout code that reads `sub` from `id_token_hint` for revocation, session lookup or back-channel logout. <sub>Identity ADR-0096</sub>
- **Resolve the pairwise sector identifier as the host of `sector_identifier_uri` when it is set, otherwise the single common host of the `redirect_uris`, otherwise the `client_id`. Never fail at issuance. At registration, reject a pairwise client whose redirect URIs span several hosts and that has no `sector_identifier_uri`.** This follows OpenID Connect Core §8.1, and the fallback still yields a stable subject that cannot be correlated. *Check:* Look for sector resolution that ignores `sector_identifier_uri`, picks one of several hosts, or throws at issuance, and for registration that accepts multi-host pairwise clients without a sector URI. <sub>Identity ADR-0093; Identity ADR-0095</sub>
- **When validating `sector_identifier_uri` at registration and update, require an absolute https URI, fetch it, require a JSON array of strings, and require every registered `redirect_uri` to appear in it by ordinal comparison. Return `invalid_client_metadata` on failure.** OpenID Connect Core §8.1 lets clients share a sector only when the owner of the document vouches for their redirect URIs. *Check:* Look for handling that accepts non-https URIs, skips the fetch, accepts non-array or non-string JSON, uses case-insensitive or prefix matching, or skips the check on update. <sub>Identity ADR-0095</sub>
- **Make the token revocation endpoint answer 200 OK to every authenticated request, whether the token was revoked, unknown, already revoked or not revocable. The only hard error is a missing or empty `token`, which returns 400 `invalid_request`.** RFC 7009 requires this leniency so the endpoint does not reveal which tokens are real. *Check:* Look for revocation handlers that return a distinct status or body based on token state, or that do not reject a missing `token`. <sub>Identity ADR-0028</sub>
- **Answer an unknown, expired, revoked or otherwise invalid token at the introspection endpoint with 200 OK and a body of only `{"active": false}`, with no other member. The only hard error is a missing `token`, which returns 400 `invalid_request`.** RFC 7662 defines this response, and extra members or error codes leak information about tokens. *Check:* Look for 4xx responses, error descriptions or claims returned for inactive tokens, and for a missing `token` answered with `active: false`. <sub>Identity ADR-0029; Identity ADR-0168</sub>
- **Report a refresh token as inactive at introspection once its family has passed its horizon, even if the store still marks the token active.** Introspection must agree with the refresh grant, which refuses such tokens with `invalid_grant`. *Check:* Look for refresh-token introspection that relies only on store state without the family horizon check. <sub>Identity ADR-0297</sub>
- **Return a JWT introspection response (RFC 9701) only to resource-server clients that list `application/token-introspection+jwt` in `Accept`, and refuse other clients that ask for it with 406. Use `typ` `token-introspection+jwt`, put only `iss`, `aud` and `iat` at the top level, nest the result under `token_introspection`, and include no top-level `sub` or `exp`.** RFC 9701 restricts JWT introspection responses to resource servers, and this shape stops the response from being mistaken for an access token. *Check:* Look for JWT introspection issued to ordinary clients, a different `typ`, flattened claims, or top-level `sub`/`exp`. <sub>Identity ADR-0168</sub>
- **Treat revocation of a stateless JWT access token as an accepted no-op, and do not add a per-token denylist lookup on the resource-server validation path unless explicitly required.** A lookup on every call defeats stateless tokens. Short lifetimes limit the exposure instead. *Check:* Look for revocation code that persists or denylists JWT access tokens, or validation that adds a revocation store lookup. <sub>Identity ADR-0028</sub>
- **When rotating a refresh token, spend it only after every validation has passed and before minting or auditing any new token. Revoke the presented grant and store its successor in a single unit of work, conditional on the presented grant still being active.** Separate steps let concurrent refreshes both succeed, or let a lineage revocation leave the successor active. Minting before the spend produces tokens that are audited but never delivered. *Check:* Look for revoke and save in separate `SaveChanges` calls, an idempotent revoke that succeeds on an already revoked grant, token creation or audit before the spend, or a spend before validation completes. <sub>Identity ADR-0211</sub>
- **When a single-use artifact (authorization code, refresh token, device code, CIBA `auth_req_id`, PAR `request_uri`, initial access token, saved flow state) loses a concurrency race on its spend, handle it exactly like a sequential second spend: the same protocol error (`invalid_grant` for codes and refresh tokens), the same replay audit, and the same side effects such as session or lineage revocation.** An uncaught lost race reached the client as a 500. RFC 9700 §4.14.2 requires the losing refresh to be treated as reuse, because the server cannot tell the attacker from the client. *Check:* Look for spend logic that saves without catching the store's concurrency exception, maps the concurrent case to a 500 or a different error, skips replay side effects, or still issues tokens. <sub>Identity ADR-0208; Identity ADR-0211</sub>
- **Answer a refresh-token retry within the reuse interval the way the rotation was answered: a new access token, an ID token when `openid` is in scope, and a new refresh token in the same lineage, without revoking the lineage or the first successor. Refuse the retry with `invalid_grant` and no replay audit or revocation when it cannot issue a refresh token, names no lineage, or the lineage has no active grant.** Revoking the head or the lineage would end the session of a client that lost the response or of a concurrent tab. A retry against a dead lineage is simply invalid, not detected reuse. *Check:* Look for retry handling that revokes the lineage, re-rotates the head, tries to return the earlier successor, issues tokens without `offline_access` or a live lineage, or records replay on the refusal. <sub>Identity ADR-0217</sub>
- **Enforce the client-level requirements the token endpoint already knows, such as a required sender constraint, before redeeming an authorization code or rotating a refresh token.** A refusal after the spend wastes the single-use code or refresh token. *Check:* Look for client requirement checks placed after code redemption or refresh rotation. <sub>Identity ADR-0158</sub>
- **For polling grants (device code, CIBA), return `slow_down` for a poll that arrives before the interval has elapsed, without advancing other request state, and record the last poll time. Return `authorization_pending` while pending, `access_denied` when denied and `expired_token` past expiry, all as HTTP 400 OAuth errors. Claim an approved request atomically, exactly once, before issuing tokens.** RFC 8628 §3.5 and CIBA define these responses, and an atomic consume stops double redemption. *Check:* Look for missing interval enforcement, a `slow_down` path that changes other state, wrong status-to-error mapping, non-400 status codes, or token issuance without an atomic consume-once. <sub>Identity ADR-0059; Identity ADR-0085</sub>
- **Normalize a device-flow `user_code` (case-fold it and strip separators and whitespace) before hashing or looking it up, and add separators only for display.** Users type the code in any case or spacing, and the lookup must match the canonical hashed form. *Check:* Look for raw `user_code` input hashed or looked up, or a display-formatted value stored or hashed. <sub>Identity ADR-0059</sub>
- **Reject a CIBA `auth_req_id` poll from a push-mode client with `unauthorized_client`.** Push clients receive tokens in the notification and never poll. *Check:* Look for CIBA grant handling that does not check the delivery mode. <sub>Identity ADR-0085</sub>
- **On a CIBA denial, notify ping or push clients exactly once, and only from the call whose own grant update decided the request. Send the notification through the same durable, retrying delivery job used for approvals, carrying no tokens. Push payloads carry `auth_req_id` and `error=access_denied` with no `error_description`. Ping payloads carry only `auth_req_id`. Poll clients receive no callback.** CIBA Core §10.2 and §12 define these payloads. Notifying from every denial call notifies twice, never notifying leaves the client waiting until expiry, and poll clients have no callback. *Check:* Look for denial paths that never notify or that notify without checking that their own update decided the request, direct HTTP calls that bypass the delivery job, token data in denial jobs, extra payload members, or callbacks sent to poll-mode clients. <sub>Identity ADR-0231</sub>
- **Validate a CIBA signed authentication request by requiring `iat`, `nbf`, `exp` and a non-empty `jti`, applying the request-object maximum lifetime, and using the client's configured clock skew instead of the JWT library's default.** CIBA Core §7.1.1 requires these claims, and validation should match the authorization endpoint. *Check:* Look for CIBA validation that does not require these claims, allows an empty `jti`, or keeps the library's default skew. <sub>Identity ADR-0187</sub>
- **For delegation token exchange, require the subject token's `may_act` to authorize the actor (its `sub` equals the actor's `sub`, and its `client_id`/`iss` match when present), reject an actor that is the same as the subject, and add an `act` claim for the actor with any existing `act` nested inside it. Do not run end-user subject validation on the actor.** RFC 8693 §4.1 and §4.4 require pre-authorization of the actor and a preserved delegation chain. The actor is not the subject the tokens are issued for. *Check:* Look for skipped or partial `may_act` checks, subject == actor allowed, an existing `act` overwritten or dropped, or subject validation run on the actor. <sub>Identity ADR-0101; Identity ADR-0225</sub>
- **In token exchange, choose the validation policy from the subject-token type: `access_token` uses the access-token policy, `id_token` uses the ID-token policy, `jwt` is accepted only if it validates as one of those, and any other type returns `invalid_request`.** This blocks the cross-JWT confusion described in RFC 9701 §8.1, such as a logout token or introspection response accepted as a subject token. *Check:* Look for a `jwt` subject token accepted without access-token or ID-token validation, or unknown types accepted. <sub>Identity ADR-0167</sub>
- **In token exchange responses, always include `issued_token_type`. Return an ID token in the `access_token` field with `token_type` `N_A`. Issue a refresh token only when a per-client setting allows it.** RFC 8693 §2.2.1 defines this response shape. *Check:* Look for a missing `issued_token_type`, an ID token returned under another field or as `Bearer`, or refresh tokens issued without the per-client check. <sub>Identity ADR-0101</sub>
- **Never hard-code `token_type = Bearer` in an issuance path. Set `token_type` and the access token's `cnf` from the proof-of-possession binding evaluated for the request, and persist `cnf` with refresh tokens so rotated tokens stay bound. Reject a bound refresh token presented without a matching proof.** Every grant must honor DPoP and mTLS binding, and RFC 9449 §5 requires binding continuity across refresh. *Check:* Look for literal `Bearer` in grant handlers, access tokens created without the request's `cnf`, refresh persistence or rotation that drops the confirmation, or refresh grants that do not compare the proof with the stored binding. <sub>Identity ADR-0097</sub>
- **Bind an access token to the mTLS client certificate only when the client's effective `require_tls_client_certificate_bound_access_tokens` is true, and refuse with `invalid_request` a client that requires binding but presents no certificate. Model server-advertised support and a client-registered requirement as separate settings, name the requirement `require_` plus its RFC client metadata member, and refuse the requirement when support is off.** Binding is opt-in. Advertised support must not force binding on every client, and a certificate used only for `tls_client_auth` does not imply binding. *Check:* Look for binding decided by the server's support flag or by the mere presence of a certificate, a silent bearer token when binding is required, or one setting used both to advertise and to force a capability. <sub>Identity ADR-0097; Identity csharp-production.instructions.md</sub>
- **Treat a required sender constraint (DPoP or mTLS) as met only when the token's `cnf` method (`jkt`, `x5t#S256`) is one that every targeted resource server verifies.** A token bound by a method the resource server does not verify is a bearer token to that server. *Check:* Look for sender-constraint checks that accept any binding without intersecting with the confirmation methods the resource servers support. <sub>Identity ADR-0158</sub>
- **When validating a DPoP proof, check that `htm` equals the request method, that `ath` matches when an access token is present, that `jti` is present, and that `iat` is within ±lifetime of now as given by `TimeProvider`. Compare `htu` with the request URI only after removing query and fragment from both and confirming both are absolute http/https URIs.** RFC 9449 defines these checks. On Unix, a rooted path such as `/token` would otherwise parse as a `file:` URI. *Check:* Look for any of these checks missing, `DateTime.UtcNow` used, raw string `htu` comparison, query or fragment kept, or no `IsAbsoluteUri`/scheme check. <sub>Identity ADR-0176</sub>
- **Create a fresh DPoP proof for every request, with header `typ: dpop+jwt`, `alg` and the public `jwk` (no `kid`), a random 128-bit `jti`, `iat` from `TimeProvider`, and `htu` stripped of query and fragment. Token-endpoint proofs use `htm` POST and have no `ath`. Resource proofs include `ath` and the cached nonce for that origin. Do not attach DPoP proofs to revocation requests.** RFC 9449 §4 and §7 require a unique proof per request and `ath` only when the proof accompanies an access token. RFC 7009 defines no DPoP for revocation. *Check:* Look for cached or reused proofs, `kid` in the header, a non-random `jti`, `DateTime.Now`, query or fragment in `htu`, `ath` on token-endpoint proofs, missing `ath` on resource proofs, or DPoP headers on revocation. <sub>Identity ADR-0176; Identity ADR-0286; Identity ADR-0291</sub>
- **When a token request carried a DPoP proof, require the response `token_type` to be `DPoP` (compared case-insensitively), and reject `Bearer` or any other value as a downgrade.** Accepting a bearer token in reply to a proof silently downgrades sender-constrained tokens. RFC 6749 §5.1 makes `token_type` case-insensitive. *Check:* Look for DPoP token response handling that does not check `token_type`, accepts `Bearer`, or compares case-sensitively. <sub>Identity ADR-0286</sub>
- **Retry a `use_dpop_nonce` challenge at most once, and only when the response carries `DPoP-Nonce`. Build the retry with a new proof, a form rebuilt from a fresh copy of the caller's parameters, client authentication run again, and request content buffered before the first send. Record `DPoP-Nonce` from every response to a proof-carrying request in a size-bounded cache keyed by origin (scheme, host, port).** Replaying the form would reuse a `private_key_jwt` assertion, unbuffered content cannot be resent, unlimited retries loop, and nonces are issued per server (RFC 9449 §8). *Check:* Look for retry loops, retries that resend the same form, proof or assertion, unbuffered `HttpContent`, ignored `DPoP-Nonce` headers on successful responses, or nonce caches keyed by full URI, held globally or unbounded. <sub>Identity ADR-0286; Identity ADR-0291; Identity ADR-0299</sub>
- **Present an access token to a resource such as UserInfo the way it was issued: with a DPoP proof of its bound key when it is DPoP-bound, as a bearer token otherwise, and over the mTLS endpoint alias when the client authenticates with mutual TLS.** RFC 9449 §7/§9 and RFC 8705 §5 require sender-constrained tokens to be presented with their proof, or the resource server rejects them. *Check:* Look for requests that always send `Authorization: Bearer`, or that skip `mtls_endpoint_aliases` resolution for mTLS clients. <sub>Identity ADR-0299</sub>
- **When a client uses mutual TLS and the provider publishes `mtls_endpoint_aliases` (RFC 8705 §5), send the request to the alias and use the alias URL for the DPoP `htu`, the nonce cache key and the authentication context. Validate every alias at discovery with the same https-or-loopback rule as other endpoints, and fail discovery if any alias fails. Always send `client_id` with `tls_client_auth` and `self_signed_tls_client_auth`.** These values must match the URL actually called, an alias receives credentials, and RFC 8705 §2 requires `client_id`. *Check:* Look for mTLS requests that ignore the alias map, DPoP or nonce values built from the non-alias URL, unvalidated alias entries, or mTLS authenticators that omit `client_id`. <sub>Identity ADR-0288</sub>
- **On the server, require each RFC 8705 mTLS endpoint alias to be an https origin (scheme, host, optional port, no path) whose host differs from the issuer's host.** Endpoints are rewritten onto the alias origin, and one host cannot both ask for a client certificate and skip it. *Check:* Check that alias validation rejects non-https values, values with a path, and a host equal to the issuer host. <sub>Identity ADR-0195</sub>
- **Require a `tls_client_auth` client to configure exactly one certificate identity setting: subject DN, or one of SAN DNS, URI, IP or email.** RFC 8705 §2.1.2 expects one expected identity, and ambiguous registrations must not authenticate. *Check:* Look for validation or matching that accepts several identity settings or ORs across them, or that accepts `tls_client_auth_*` parameters for other methods. <sub>Identity ADR-0107; Identity ADR-0145</sub>
- **When parsing an Envoy `X-Forwarded-Client-Cert` header, read only the first element (added by the proxy closest to the client), honor quoting and backslash escapes, prefer `Chain`, and require `Cert` to equal the leaf of `Chain` when both are present.** The first element identifies the real client, and a `Cert` that disagrees with `Chain` is inconsistent input. *Check:* Look for parsing that takes the last element, splits on commas or semicolons without handling quotes, or accepts a `Cert` that differs from the leaf. <sub>Identity ADR-0172</sub>
- **When client authentication fails and credentials were sent in the `Authorization` header (for example `client_secret_basic`), return 401 with a `WWW-Authenticate` challenge for that scheme (for example `Basic realm="<issuer>"`). Keep 400 `invalid_client` for body and assertion methods. Reject Basic credentials that contain no colon as malformed.** RFC 6749 §5.2 requires the 401 challenge in the header case, and RFC 7617 §2 defines the user-pass format. *Check:* Look for Basic failures returned as 400 or without `WWW-Authenticate`, body or assertion methods answered with 401, or Basic parsing that accepts a value with no colon. <sub>Identity ADR-0092; Identity ADR-0145</sub>
- **For JWT-bearer client authentication on the server, identify the client from the assertion's `sub` without requiring a `client_id` parameter, accept `aud` only when it equals the issuer or the receiving endpoint URL, and reject an `alg` outside the configured `token_endpoint_auth_signing_alg_values_supported`.** FAPI `private_key_jwt` clients send only the assertion. FAPI 2.0 requires the issuer as audience and OIDC Core §9 permits the endpoint URL. Advertised algorithms must match those accepted. *Check:* Look for rejection when `client_id` is absent, client resolution from `client_id`, audience checks that accept only one value or anything, or a supported-algorithm list that is ignored. <sub>Identity ADR-0102</sub>
- **When building a `private_key_jwt` client assertion on the client, set `aud` to the OP issuer as a single string, `iss` and `sub` to the client id, `jti` to 16 random bytes in base64url, `iat`/`nbf` to now, and `exp` to a fixed short lifetime (60 seconds). For `client_secret_basic`, form-urlencode the client id and the secret before joining them with `:` and base64-encoding.** RFC 7523bis and FAPI 2.0 require the issuer as audience, and RFC 6749 §2.3.1 requires the encoding. *Check:* Look for an assertion `aud` set to the token endpoint or an array, a non-random `jti`, a long or configurable lifetime, or Basic headers built from raw `client_id:secret`. <sub>Identity ADR-0270</sub>
- **Configure a confidential OAuth or BFF client to use authorization code with PKCE S256, `private_key_jwt` or mTLS client authentication, PAR when advertised, RFC 9207 `iss` validation, and DPoP when the provider supports it. Do not implement implicit, hybrid or password flows, or token-mediating backends that hand access tokens to the browser.** These are the protections the OAuth security BCP and the BFF guidance require, and the excluded flows expose tokens to script. *Check:* Look for `client_secret` as the default auth, PAR or DPoP unused when advertised, `response_type` values containing `token`/`id_token`, `grant_type=password`, or endpoints that return access tokens to the SPA. *Note:* This applies to relying-party/BFF client code. The OpenID Provider itself may still implement front-channel logout and session management (see the logout rules). <sub>Identity docs/backend-for-frontend.md</sub>
- **Make relying-party and BFF client code depend only on standard provider metadata, endpoints and client registration (for example RFC 7591, RFC 9126, RFC 9449). Require at least one `redirect_uri` for redirect-based grants. Return `invalid_redirect_uri` only for `redirect_uris` violations and `invalid_client_metadata` for everything else, including `post_logout_redirect_uris`.** RFC 7591 §2 and §3.2.2 define these defaults and error codes, and storing an invalid client makes every later request fail. *Check:* Look for metadata persisted without domain validation, inconsistent defaults, missing `redirect_uris` checks, or `invalid_redirect_uri` used for other fields. <sub>Identity ADR-0063; Identity ADR-0140; Identity ADR-0141; Identity ADR-0203; Identity ADR-0206</sub>
- **Require a redirect URI to be absolute with no fragment (any scheme, so native apps work). Require a `backchannel_logout_uri` to be absolute https with no fragment. Require `frontchannel_logout_uri` and `post_logout_redirect_uris` to be absolute http/https with no fragment, with the front-channel URI's origin matching a registered redirect URI. Require `jwks_uri`, `sector_identifier_uri` and `client_notification_endpoint` to be https.** Each URI must be usable and safe. A `logout_token` must not travel in clear text, and Front-Channel Logout requires the origin match. *Check:* Look for relative URIs or fragments accepted, http allowed for back-channel logout or key URIs, or a front-channel URI accepted without the origin check. *Note:* ADR-0140 allows http or https for logout URIs in general. The more specific ADR-0063 requires https for back-channel logout, which is kept here. <sub>Identity ADR-0063; Identity ADR-0140</sub>
- **In dynamic registration, store each response type canonical and deduplicated, and report it back the same way, with an empty `response_types` list reported explicitly. Report `scope` as the scopes the client can request now, taken from entitlements, and do not store the requested scope. Ignore server-set or unknown metadata members instead of rejecting them.** RFC 7591 §2 and §3.2.1 require these behaviors. An omitted `response_types` reads as `code`, and a client that echoes its read response back in an update must not fail. *Check:* Look for rewritten, non-canonical or duplicate response types, an omitted empty list, the requested scope persisted or echoed back, or errors raised on read-only or unknown members. <sub>Identity ADR-0139; Identity ADR-0141; Identity ADR-0192</sub>
- **In dynamic registration, refuse an auth method outside the tenant's effective ceiling with `invalid_client_metadata`, and require the material the method verifies against: `jwks`/`jwks_uri` for `private_key_jwt`, certificates (`x5c` when `jwks` is given by value) for `self_signed_tls_client_auth`, and exactly one `tls_client_auth_*` parameter for `tls_client_auth`. Classifying methods by name misjudges methods added by packages. *Check:* Look for methods accepted without ceiling or material checks, or secret issuance decided from a fixed list of method names. <sub>Identity ADR-0145; Identity ADR-0207</sub>
- **Validate response-protection client metadata consistently: an `*_enc` requires its `*_alg`, encryption requires `jwks` or `jwks_uri`, each value must be in the matching `*_values_supported`, and a client that is not eligible for that response gets `invalid_client_metadata`.** Registration must refuse protection the server cannot honor. *Check:* Look for new signed or encrypted response metadata accepted without these checks. <sub>Identity ADR-0192</sub>
- **Give a client's public keys exactly one source, either stored keys or `jwks_uri`, never merged. Fail closed, resolving no keys, when the `jwks_uri` fetch fails or the set is refused. Refuse with 409 any write that would create both. Treat an RFC 7592 update as a full replacement: its `jwks` replaces the stored public keys, a `jwks_uri` removes them, and shared secrets are kept.** OIDC Dynamic Registration §2 forbids both sources, and a merge or an untouched update lets stale keys outlive a rotation. *Check:* Look for merged key resolution, fallback to stored keys on fetch failure, consumers that bypass the shared resolver, writes without the conflict check, or updates that leave keys or delete shared secrets. <sub>Identity ADR-0161</sub>
- **Make a registered JWK Set all-or-nothing, so any unusable key is `invalid_client_metadata`. For a fetched `jwks_uri` set, skip keys with an unknown type or algorithm, no `kid`, bad formatting or contradictory metadata (RFC 7517 §5), but refuse the whole set if it contains private or symmetric material or two usable keys with the same `kid`.** A registered unusable key never works. A published set may serve others, but a compromised or ambiguous set must never be used. *Check:* Look for registration that silently drops keys, a fetched set rejected over one unsupported key, or only the offending key skipped when private material or a duplicate `kid` is present. <sub>Identity ADR-0161</sub>
- **Keep an imported JWK's `kid` as the key's identifier for signing and selection, separate from the stored resource id. Fall back to the internal id only when the key has no `kid`, and never use a client-supplied `kid` as a global primary key.** Relying parties select keys by the publisher's `kid` (RFC 7517 §4.5), and using `kid` as a resource id collides across clients and tenants. *Check:* Look for import code that drops the `kid`, replaces it with a generated id, or uses it as the entity's primary identifier. <sub>Identity ADR-0161; Identity ADR-0186</sub>

- **Export an EC JWK's `crv` from the key's actual curve OID, falling back to the key size only when the curve cannot be resolved.** Guessing from the size misnames curves that share a size with a NIST curve. *Check:* Look for `crv` set from `KeySize` alone instead of `ECParameters.Curve.Oid`. <sub>Identity ADR-0068</sub>
- **For ML-DSA (AKP) JWKs, write `priv` as the 32-byte seed only and `pub` as the raw public key, always export `alg` and require it on import, and use `alg`, `kty`, `pub` as thumbprint members (RFC 9964). - **Compute `at_hash`, `c_hash` and `s_hash` with the signing algorithm's token-hash function: SHA-512 for Ed25519, SHAKE256 with 114 bytes of output for Ed448, and the key's curve for polymorphic `EdDSA`. RFC 9864 deprecates `EdDSA` but does not prohibit it, and removing it breaks interop. *Check:* Look for token hashes derived from `HashAlgorithmName` or SHA-512 assumed for all EdDSA keys, or `EdDSA` unregistered or rejected. <sub>Identity ADR-0272</sub>

When a JWE header replicates `iss`, require it to be a string equal to the expected issuer.** RFC 7519 §1, §5.2 and §5.3 define these rules, and a replicated value that disagrees with the issuer must not be trusted. *Check:* Look for JSON-serialized JWS/JWE accepted, a missing `cty`, or a replicated `iss` that is ignored or not compared. <sub>Identity ADR-0154; Identity ADR-0280</sub>
- **Read NumericDate claims (`exp`, `nbf`, `iat`, `auth_time`) only as JSON numbers that may be fractional, through the NumericDate accessors, never as integer-only values or as date strings.** RFC 7519 allows fractional NumericDates, and parsing date strings compares local ticks against UTC. *Check:* Look for `TryGetInt64`/`GetInt64` or `TryGetValue<DateTimeOffset>` used on time claims. <sub>Identity ADR-0123</sub>
- **Truncate instants that a JWT or stored grant carries to whole seconds with the `NCode.Time` helpers (`GetUtcNowWithPrecisionInSeconds`, `GetTimestampWithPrecisionInSeconds`, `WithPrecisionInSeconds`), not with inline tick arithmetic.** A stored time must equal the NumericDate it round-trips through. *Check:* Look for `Ticks % TimeSpan.TicksPerSecond`, hand-rolled truncation, or raw `TimeProvider.GetUtcNow()` used for token or grant times. <sub>Identity ADR-0188; Identity csharp-production.instructions.md</sub>
- **When decoding JSON into claims, keep a JSON string as `ClaimValueTypes.String` with its exact value and never infer a date or number from its shape. Type a JSON number by keeping its raw text and choosing the most specific match: integer32, integer64, uinteger64, unbounded integer, and double only when the number has a fraction or exponent.** Sniffing alters signed data (for example an OIDC `birthdate`), and probing narrow-to-wide with overwrites types everything as double and loses integers above 2^53. *Check:* Look for string claims run through date or number detection, double probed before the integer types, later probes overwriting earlier ones, or reformatted number text. <sub>Identity ADR-0121; Identity ADR-0122</sub>
- **Encode each declared claim value type to its JSON type: uinteger types as unsigned numbers, unbounded integer as the narrowest long/ulong or an exact JSON number, `JSON_NULL` as null, and `JSON`/`JSON_ARRAY` only when well formed and of the declared kind. - **Never parse an empty HTTP response body as JSON, and parse JSON only for the expected JSON media types.** Valid responses, such as a successful RFC 7009 revocation, can be empty. *Check:* Look for deserialization without empty-body or media-type checks. <sub>Identity ADR-0270</sub>
- **Answer a rate-limited or over-quota request with 429, the `temporarily_unavailable` error code, a `Retry-After` header in whole seconds (rounded up, at least 1) until the window resets, and `Cache-Control: no-store`, using the same shape for every limiter, and do not run the handler.** RFC 6585 §4 and RFC 9110 §10.2.3 define this response, and a uniform shape lets clients handle all limits the same way. *Check:* Look for other status or error codes, a missing, date-valued, fractional, rounded-down or zero `Retry-After`, a missing no-store, or a handler that still runs. <sub>Identity ADR-0196; Identity ADR-0198</sub>
- **Evaluate narrower or per-minute limits before broader limits and daily quotas, so a refusal never spends a later counter. Judge overage against the quota's own shared counter at admission. Exempt public metadata endpoints (discovery, JWKS) from quotas and metering.** Refused or anonymous requests must not be billed or spend quota, and a lagging ledger or second counter misstates overage. *Check:* Look for quotas incremented before short-window limits, overage taken from ledger totals or a separate counter, direct or duplicated meter recording, or discovery and JWKS metered. <sub>Identity ADR-0198; Identity ADR-0200; Identity ADR-0246; Identity csharp-production.instructions.md</sub>
- **Align rate-limit windows to multiples of their length counted from the first tick of `DateTimeOffset`, so daily windows are UTC calendar days, and allow overage only on fixed windows.** Aligned UTC windows give the same boundaries on every replica, and tenants cannot reset a quota by changing time zone. *Check:* Look for windows computed from local time, tenant time zones, `DateTime.Now`, the request time, or a rolling 24 hours, or an overage on a sliding window. <sub>Identity ADR-0198; Identity ADR-0246</sub>

- **Do not emit an `ETag` or concurrency token for a representation assembled from several persisted entities. - **In content negotiation, implement the default representation (JSON) as a formatter in the same pipeline and make it the final fallback. Choose an alternate formatter only for an explicit supported type/subtype, so `*/*` or `type/*` gets the default.** JSON stays the OAuth/OIDC wire default for programmatic callers. *Check:* Look for inline fallback branches outside the formatter collection, or wildcard Accept values matching HTML or other alternates. <sub>Identity ADR-0114</sub>
- **Return 404 for a public-key read on a symmetric secret, and never return symmetric material from a public-key endpoint.** A symmetric secret has no public half. *Check:* Look for public-key endpoints that return 200 with empty data, 400, or secret material for symmetric secrets. <sub>Identity ADR-0058</sub>
- **Serve the interactive login and consent surface from the OP's own origin, submit its forms as native HTML form POSTs, and plug it in through an ASP.NET Core authentication scheme (matching scheme name and `LoginPath`) instead of changing the authorize/authenticate/challenge pipeline.** The cookie redirect, antiforgery, Set-Cookie and ReturnUrl round-trip only work cleanly on the same origin, and the UI is a form surface, not a new authentication model. *Check:* Look for login pages hosted on another origin, submissions made with fetch/axios, or UI changes that bypass `ChallengeAsync`/`AuthenticateAsync`. <sub>Identity ADR-0062; Identity ADR-0065</sub>

- **Make a message broadcast between replicas carry only an identifier as a hint, and have each receiver re-read the committed state from the store.** Broadcasts can be lost, repeated or late. *Check:* Look for pub/sub payloads that carry entity state for receivers to apply directly. <sub>Identity ADR-0219</sub>
- **Read and write a defined little-endian wire encoding with `BinaryPrimitives.Read/Write…LittleEndian`, not `MemoryMarshal.Read<T>/Write<T>`.** `MemoryMarshal` uses the host's endianness. *Check:* Look for `MemoryMarshal.Read/Write` used on fixed-endian data without an endianness guard. <sub>Identity ADR-0116</sub>
- **When building a query string by hand, percent-encode each name and value with `Uri.EscapeDataString`, and join to the endpoint with `?`, or with `&` when it already has a query.** This is correct RFC 3986 encoding, and existing queries are preserved. *Check:* Look for unencoded concatenation, `HttpUtility`/`WebUtility.UrlEncode`, or an unconditional `?`. <sub>Identity ADR-0285</sub>
- **Load protocol endpoint requests into strongly-typed request models backed by known parameter definitions instead of hand-rolled `form.TryGetValue`/`Request.Form[...]` reads, and keep endpoints thin: guard the verb and content type, authenticate the client through the shared service, run validation steps, and render.** Typed requests give consistent parsing, extensibility and OpenAPI metadata, and keep protocol steps replaceable. *Check:* Look for direct form or query reads, or inline validation in endpoint code. <sub>Identity ADR-0086; Identity csharp-production.instructions.md</sub>
- **Refer to OAuth/OIDC parameter names and values, and HTTP status codes, through shared named constants (status codes named like ASP.NET Core `StatusCodes`) instead of inline string literals, `(int)HttpStatusCode.X` casts or bare numbers.** One vocabulary prevents typos and client/server mismatches. *Check:* Look for literal protocol field names in builders or parsers, and for enum casts or magic numbers in status comparisons. <sub>Identity review of #350; Identity ADR-0285</sub>
- **Give a JSON-deserialized wire DTO a `[JsonExtensionData] Dictionary<string, JsonElement>? ExtensionData` member.** Unrecognized members then round-trip instead of being dropped. *Check:* Look for new deserialized DTOs without an extension data bag. <sub>Identity csharp-production.instructions.md</sub>
- **When an API-reference renderer (Scalar/OpenAPI) logs in with client credentials, send them where the client's registered auth method expects (for example the Authorization header for `client_secret_basic`).
